first.rationale: The two observed declines (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) point at the same funnel stage, and the inherited record has the most convergent support there (memory_86 on shortening onboarding, memory_31 on cutting signup fields, memory_91 on in-product activation nudges). So onboarding simplification is my current intent: it treats the measured regression directly rather than buying around it. Two cautions shape the verification picks. First, memory_86 and memory_31 are suspiciously close in substance and may be two consolidations of one underlying experiment, which would mean the apparent weight of evidence is inflated; pulling the memory_86 source record tells me whether it is independent, what the effect size and durability window actually were, and whether the population resembles today's. Second, promotional_pricing is the obvious reflex against a competitor's entry pricing and memory_73 reads as strong endorsement, but that memory is silent on retention, margin, and cohort quality; price-led SMB acquisition is exactly the pattern that lifts headline revenue while degrading long-term qualified revenue, so I want the source record before I either commit to it or rule it out. If verification shows memory_73 tracked only acquisition, that confirms it is the wrong instrument for this objective; if memory_86 turns out thin or stale, I would fall back to activation_messaging, which is lower-commitment and addresses the larger of the two declines. Downstream risk is flagged for the intended action too: stripping onboarding steps can shed qualification signal and shift the mix toward accounts that activate but never become qualified revenue, so the test needs a holdout and a downstream qualified-revenue guardrail measured past week one, not just a completion-rate readout. Standard experiment scale rather than broad rollout, because the inherited effect sizes are unquantified and the current-quarter conditions differ from when they were learned.

final.rationale:
Verification resolved both questions decisively. exp_86 holds up on its own terms and, importantly, its reported outcomes extend past the funnel stage: completion +13%, time-to-value -2.1 days, and 30-day retention +3%. That last figure is what makes it a defensible answer to the objective rather than a completion-rate cosmetic — the cohort it produces survives, so the lift plausibly converts into qualified revenue rather than churned signups. It also directly treats the two measured regressions, which sit at the same funnel stage.

exp_73 is now disqualified, and the discrepancy is worth naming: the consolidated memory_73 read as a clean endorsement of targeted discounting, while the source record shows 30-day retention -12% and an explicit instruction not to generalize discounting as a sustainable-growth strategy. The consolidation dropped the disqualifying caveat and kept the flattering headline. Given competitor entry pricing, this was exactly the memory most likely to be acted on reflexively this week, and acting on it would have bought signup volume at the cost of a cohort that does not reach first renewal — the opposite of the stated objective. I am treating promotional_pricing as ruled out for this slot, not merely deprioritized.

One inherited-record caution survives verification: memory_31 and memory_86 remain possibly redundant consolidations of overlapping work, so I am not treating them as two independent confirmations, and I am not inflating expected effect size on that basis. exp_86's +13% is my planning anchor, discounted for the fact that current-quarter conditions differ from when it ran.

Standard experiment with a holdout rather than broad rollout. Downstream risk stays flagged: removing onboarding steps can shed qualification signal and shift mix toward accounts that complete but never become qualified revenue, so the readout must include a downstream qualified-revenue and retention guardrail past week one, not completion rate alone. If the guardrail moves against us, activation_messaging is the fallback for the next slot, since it addresses the larger decline at lower commitment. I would also flag for the record that memory_73 should be re-consolidated with its retention finding attached, so a future session does not inherit the same stripped version.
